title: packages: the served package row carries no "may be disabled" verdict, so the Console cannot offer Disable on a suite module the server now accepts
body:
domain:server#2 · os-project-manager · session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo

Filing gate: out-of-scope finding (class b) in the #28117 os-dev-report `6538834934` (PR #28308). Card item 4 asked for it to be reported as a Seam, not written. Filed by `domain:server` seat 2. ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets the lane and grade.

Reach: a customer admin on the Packages page (Setup → Installed Apps opens the same view), who wants to switch off a suite module. PR #28308 lets the server's disable door accept such a module. The Console still cannot offer the action, because it shows Disable only on `writable` rows, and `writable` stays `false` for a module.
Reader who acts: `domain:spec` for the served key in `packages/spec/src/api/package-api-assembled.zod.ts`, then `domain:server` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`) to serve it. The Console half is #28118, which is `Blocked-by` this card in effect.

## What the code does (read, not measured)

- `SERVED_ROW_VERDICTS` in `package-api-assembled.zod.ts` declares one server verdict on a served package row, `writable`: "may an org author into and manage this package". `withWritableVerdict` in the runtime's `packages.ts` serves it from `isWritablePackage`.
- After PR #28308, the disable door asks `isDisableableAppModule` first (a `type: 'module'` package directly depending on an installed `type: 'app'` package, own scope not `system`/`cloud`), so it accepts a disable that `writable` says no to. No served key carries that answer.
- `PackagesPage.tsx` L1054 renders Disable / Enable on `writable || !enabled`. So the server accepts a disable that the Console cannot offer. #28117's item 4 and #28118's item 1 both say the Console must not re-derive the rule (#8146: one answer, served by the server), and ⛔ `writable` must not be overloaded.

## Wanted (route is triage's)

- A served verdict beside `writable` that answers "may this package be disabled here?", computed by the same predicate the disable door asks. The name and shape are the spec lane's call, for example a boolean `disableable`.
- The runtime serves it on every row door that serves `writable`.
- #28118 then reads it.
- This is a new public key, so `Clause-②: yes` and a contract review.

## Dedupe

Dedupe words: served verdict disable module, SERVED_ROW_VERDICTS disableable, Packages page disable module. I read the open issues updated since 10-30 for `28117`, `SERVED_ROW_VERDICTS` and `disableable`. Only #28285 (the ADR line) and #28118 (the Console half, which assumes this key) cite it. **New.**

Links back: #28117, PR #28308, #28118, #8146
